actions.body: Research on the sunk cost effect [source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca] demonstrates that intelligence often persists in failing paths due to prior resource commitment. This bias is exacerbated in planning tasks, where goal-directed agents treat current actions as rigid prerequisites [source-4fb70d1c1dd147da]. To mitigate this, we propose integrating adaptive evaluation frameworks—borrowed from conservation planning [source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb]—to formalize stopping rules that prioritize epistemic return over historical investment.
actions.lede: Question abandonment in research requires moving beyond simple sunk cost logic toward adaptive evaluation frameworks.
